description: Curated reference statements used by the fact-check step. A mock stand-in for an agency research database; every entry carries a source and an as-of date so stale facts can be flagged.

entries.statement: GitLab is an all-remote company with no offices. It publishes its company handbook publicly at handbook.gitlab.com; the handbook runs to thousands of pages and covers processes, values and how work gets done.

Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com and Tumblr, has been fully distributed since its founding in 2005 and closed its San Francisco office in 2017. It documents its way of working in the Automattic Creed and an internal field guide; its handbook is mostly internal rather than published like GitLab's.

Doist, the maker of Todoist and Twist, is a remote-first company with roughly 100 employees across more than 30 countries. It publicly advocates async-first communication and has published guides on remote and asynchronous work.

entries.topic: Share of remote work days in the US
entries.statement: According to the Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes (WFH Research), roughly a quarter of paid full workdays in the US were worked from home through 2024 and 2025, down from a peak above 60% in spring 2020 and far above the roughly 5% pre-pandemic level.

Several large employers tightened office mandates in 2024-2025; for example Amazon required corporate employees to work from the office five days a week starting January 2, 2025. Hybrid arrangements remain the most common pattern for remote-capable jobs.
entries.source: Amazon - message from CEO Andy Jassy (Sept 2024)

entries.statement: Surveys consistently show many workers value remote or hybrid flexibility and employers offering it widen their hiring pool, but evidence that remote-first firms dominate hiring overall is not established.
entries.source: WFH Research; Gallup hybrid work indicators

entries.statement: The FDA maintains a public list of AI-enabled medical devices it has authorized; the list passed 1,000 devices by 2025. Roughly three quarters are in radiology, and most were cleared through the 510(k) pathway, with others via De Novo or PMA review.

In April 2018 the FDA granted De Novo authorization to IDx-DR (now LumineticsCore), the first AI system authorized to give a screening decision for diabetic retinopathy without a clinician interpreting the image. Autonomous AI diagnostics therefore already exist in narrow use cases.

entries.topic: AI triage of urgent imaging findings
entries.statement: Hospitals use FDA-authorized computer-aided triage software to flag urgent findings on imaging, such as Viz.ai's stroke (large vessel occlusion) alerting, authorized in 2018, and Aidoc's tools for CT findings. These systems prioritise worklists for radiologists rather than replacing their reads.

Health systems deploy symptom checker and digital triage tools (for example from Ada Health, Infermedica and Buoy Health) on websites and apps to guide patients to an appropriate level of care before a visit.
entries.source: Vendor deployment announcements; peer-reviewed evaluations of symptom checkers

entries.statement: COVID-19 sharply accelerated digital health adoption: McKinsey estimated in 2021 that telehealth use had stabilised at about 38 times the pre-pandemic baseline.
entries.source: McKinsey & Company, 'Telehealth: A quarter-trillion-dollar post-COVID-19 reality?' (July 2021)

entries.statement: Obermeyer et al. (Science, 2019) showed that a widely used commercial algorithm for managing patient health under-identified Black patients for extra care because it used past healthcare cost as a proxy for need, a well-documented example of bias learned from historical clinical data.
In the US, protected health information is governed by HIPAA; using patient data to train or run AI systems raises privacy and consent obligations for covered entities and their business associates.

US interoperability policy is built on the 21st Century Cures Act (2016), the ONC information-blocking rules and the HL7 FHIR standard. TEFCA, the national framework for exchanging health information, went live in December 2023.

Most FDA-authorized AI tools are labelled as aids to clinicians (computer-aided detection, triage or decision support); final diagnostic and treatment decisions generally remain with a licensed clinician.
entries.source: FDA - Clinical Decision Support Software guidance (2022)

entries.statement: Mailchimp grew without venture capital and was acquired by Intuit for about $12 billion in cash and stock in 2021, a frequently cited example of a bootstrapped company reaching a large outcome.
Atlassian was founded in 2002 and self-funded for about eight years before taking its first outside investment, a $60 million round from Accel in 2010.

Founders typically sell around 20% of the company in a priced seed round and a similar share in Series A, according to Carta data, so venture funding dilutes founder ownership and control over successive rounds.
entries.source: Carta - State of Private Markets / dilution data

entries.topic: VC fund lifecycle and exit pressure
entries.statement: Venture capital funds commonly have a roughly 10-year term (often with extensions), which creates pressure for portfolio companies to reach a liquidity event such as an acquisition or IPO within that window.

Venture capital is designed to fund rapid growth ahead of revenue in large markets; most startups never raise venture capital, and bootstrapped firms typically grow more slowly but keep full ownership.
entries.source: Harvard Business School Online - bootstrapping vs. venture capital

entries.statement: NASA's Mars Sample Return campaign has faced major cost and schedule overruns; in 2024 NASA said its original plan was too expensive and slow, and sought alternative architectures, with sample return no earlier than the 2030s. Perseverance continues to cache samples on Mars.
